sentences.text: Linheraptor was a small, bird-like theropod dromaeosaurid that lived in what is now China during the Late Cretaceous. This bipedal carnivore measured approximately 1.8 meters in length and weighed up to 25 kilograms. Like other members of its group, it possessed an elongated skull, a curved neck, a long tail, and enlarged toe claws.
The species name exquisitus refers to the excellent preservation of the holotype specimen, which is the specific fossil the species is based on.
Despite its modest size, this animal was likely a fast and agile predator capable of hunting small ceratopsians.

The genus Linheraptor was named by Xu Xing and colleagues in 2010 to honor the Linhe district in Inner Mongolia. A nearly complete fossilized skeleton was found in 2008 by Jonah N. Choiniere and Michael Pittman in the Wulansuhai Formation at Bayan Mandahu.
Researchers suggest the large toe claws of Linheraptor may have been used for capturing prey.
Linheraptor is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae and the subfamily Velociraptorinae. It and the genus Tsaagan are considered intermediate forms between basal and derived dromaeosaurids.
The fossil record for Linheraptor spans the Campanian age, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago. It lived approximately 75 million years ago in what is now Asia.
It is debated whether Linheraptor exquisitus is a junior synonym of Tsaagan mangas; some researchers argue for synonymy while others reject it based on anatomical details.
